name: Gabriel hounds

attributes.attribute: were spectral dogs that could disguise as wild geese
foretold death or disaster by circling a house
was the source of the name Gabriel in this folk belief
were not linked to the Christian archangel

sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
response: The “Gabriel” to whom the hounds belonged is another name for Gwynn Ap Nudd, the Welsh king of the Otherworld, and does not refer to the Christian archangel.
text: Gabriel hounds were spectral dogs in British folklore. Sources also name them Gabriel ratchets, gaze hounds, and lyme hounds. The dogs could pass as migrating wild geese. They flew overhead and barked in voices like birdcalls. A circling pack over a house foretold death or disaster. The old word ratchet means a hunting hound. The name Gabriel belonged to Gwynn ap Nudd, the Welsh king of the Otherworld. It did not name the Christian archangel.

okr.objective: Record the British belief in the spectral Gabriel hounds.
